claims.text: Introducing a controlled amount of lattice distortion through alloying can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Boron or carbon additions can induce lattice distortion in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Suitable processing conditions can preserve the eutectic microstructure after the alloying addition.
The alloying addition produces lattice distortion.
The resulting lattice distortion changes dislocation dynamics.
Lattice distortion increases strength by hindering dislocation movement.
Preservation of the eutectic microstructure maintains or enhances ductility by facilitating strain hardening.
Preservation of the eutectic microstructure maintains or enhances ductility by facilitating crack blunting.
The intervention will increase yield strength by at least 10% relative to the as-cast alloy without the addition.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by at least 5% relative to the as-cast alloy without the addition.
The simultaneous improvement is limited to alloys that retain a eutectic microstructure and have lattice distortion within a suitable range.
Lattice distortion outside the suitable range may make the alloy too brittle or too soft.
